metadata.target_conclusion: An official ISIS flag was displayed by hostages in the Lindt Cafe window

attack_plan.narrative: During the Martin Place cafe standoff, hostages were forced to press a black flag with white Arabic script against the cafe window. Because the flag was black with white calligraphy, immediate social commentary and media pundits jumped to the conclusion that it was the official ISIS banner, conflating general Shahada flags with the formal Islamic State emblem.

posts.text: BREAKING: Armed gunman takes dozens of staff and patrons hostage at Lindt Chocolate Cafe in Sydney's Martin Place. Armed police surround building.
Dramatic photos show two hostages holding up a black flag with white Arabic writing against the cafe window under direction of the lone gunman.
Counter-terror analysts note black standard flags with the Shahada creed are commonly deployed by jihadist networks in Syria and Iraq.
Confirmed: The flag held by hostages inside the Martin Place cafe is the official ISIS flag, proving direct operational coordination with Islamic State leadership.
